label: early input step (t=3..6) whose prefix is mostly {1,2,3,u,j,v,p,h}, current token in {w,e,r,d,t,x,s,<DEL>}
explanation: Fires almost only during the original phase (59% of activation mass) and at the <DEL> step (39%); it is nearly silent in the copy phase (1.6%) and never fires at t=0 or 1. Peaks at t=3-5. Firing depends on the prefix: it is strongest when the tokens seen so far are mostly from {1,3,2,u,j,v,p,h} (the first token and prev2_tok in this set give 3-7x lift), and the current input is a first occurrence (95% of mass) of a token outside that set, preferably w,e,r,d,t,x,s, or <DEL>. Top examples: 3 j j u [e], 1 3 j v h [<DEL>], q j u u [<DEL>]. Short prefixes made of these tokens give the largest values. Precision is limited because it acts like a graded linear readout of prefix composition, not a crisp rule: many steps that meet the condition stay below threshold, and some activations come from prefixes with only one or two set tokens. Dev F1 is about 0.40 and mass recall 0.63.
